Inside the Night Shift at the Airport

At two in the morning the departures hall is almost empty. A cleaner pushes a wide mop past the closed coffee stands, and the boards flicker through tomorrow's first flights to cities that are still asleep.

Behind the walls, though, the airport never stops. Baggage belts run, fuel trucks circle the aprons, and a small team in the control tower keeps watch over a sky that is quieter than it will be for the rest of the day.

We spent a week with the people who keep it running while everyone else sleeps, and what we found was not quiet at all.
